findings.highlight: It must be luck that I avoided it.
findings.evidenceJa: それを避けられたのは偶然か
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether avoiding the dagger-like object was chance.
findings.explanation: An open question becomes a confident explanation.

findings.highlight: I could have shown you my full secret technique
findings.evidenceJa: 秘剣の全てを味わえた
findings.governingReading: Assassin says he could have savored the whole of Saber’s secret technique.
findings.explanation: The English reverses who would experience whose secret technique.

findings.evidenceJa: ぼう、と立ち尽くしている
findings.governingReading: Saber stands motionless in a blank or dazed state.
findings.explanation: The English keeps the posture but removes the marked mental state.

findings.highlight: I’ll bring it up when you wake up
findings.evidenceJa: 目を覚ましたらとっちめてやる
findings.governingReading: Shirou mutters that he will give Saber a proper scolding when she wakes.
findings.explanation: A mock-threatening comic promise is reduced to merely mentioning the subject.

findings.highlight: Why are you looking at me if you’ve seen a ghost?
findings.evidenceJa: お化けでも見たような顔しちゃって
findings.governingReading: Rin asks why Shirou looks as though he has seen a ghost.
findings.explanation: The malformed conditional makes seeing a ghost the reason he should look at Rin.

findings.highlight: We noticed the presence of a third Servant
findings.evidenceJa: 第三のサーヴァントに気が付き
findings.governingReading: Saber says that she noticed the third Servant observing their battle.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the detection to both combatants instead of Saber.

findings.highlight: if I’m going to let you fight, I’m going to fight myself
findings.evidenceJa: おまえに戦わせるぐらいなら、俺が自分で戦う
findings.governingReading: Rather than make Saber fight, Shirou says he will fight himself.
findings.explanation: The English conditional can mean that he will let her fight and join her, reversing the substitution at the center of his claim.

findings.highlight: I can’t allow someone to get hurt, In place of saving me.
findings.evidenceJa: 無力な自分を守って。その代わりに“誰か”が傷つくのは許せない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot accept someone being hurt in exchange for protecting his powerless self.
findings.explanation: Broken syntax obscures the exchange relation that connects his survivor psychology to his justice ideal.

findings.highlight: It looks this conversation is going nowhere
findings.governingReading: The conversation appears to be going nowhere.
findings.explanation: The English omits the required “like” or “as though,” producing malformed prose.

findings.governingReading: For anything one undertakes, the body or health is the essential capital.
findings.explanation: A Japanese proverb is copied into an opaque English claim about bodily origin.
